families.why: The __slots__ change only affects instance attribute storage; evaluating a trivial marker exercises the fast path (single tuple, no nesting, no extras). Any speed‑up from slot access shows up here.
families.size_meaning: Number of markers created and evaluated (each marker string length grows modestly with n).
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # produce n markers of slowly increasing length
    base = "python_version >= '3.'"
    return [[base + str(i % 10) + "'"] for i in range(1, n + 1)]

families.why: The added __slots__ eliminates the instance __dict__, making Marker construction and attribute access faster. This family creates many tiny, valid marker strings to exercise object creation and evaluation.
families.size_meaning: n is the number of Marker instances created and evaluated
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # Simple, always‑true marker to keep evaluation cheap
    base = "python_version >= '3.0'"
    return [[base] for _ in range(n)]

families.why: Adding __slots__ removes the per‑instance __dict__, making object allocation and attribute write/read of _markers faster. Creating a large number of Marker objects therefore benefits from the change.
families.size_meaning: number of Marker objects created (each with a trivial marker expression)
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # generate n distinct but simple marker strings
    base = "python_version >= '3.{0}'"
    return [[base.format(i % 10)] for i in range(1, n + 1)]

families.family: Deeply nested marker expressions with many 'and'/'or' groups
families.why: Parsing creates a large recursive MarkerList structure. The __slots__ addition does not change parsing cost, but the extra attribute‑lookup overhead for each node (now via slot) can marginally increase per‑node work when the evaluator walks a very deep tree.
families.size_meaning: Nesting depth proportional to n (each level adds an 'or' group).
families.make_source:
def make(n):
    # Build a left‑deep expression: a or (a or (a or ...))
    atom = "python_version == '3.8'"
    expr = atom
    for i in range(n):
        expr = f"{atom} or ({expr})"
    return [[expr]]

families.why: A marker with many nested ``or`` groups forces the evaluator to allocate many intermediate lists. The __slots__ change does not affect parsing but could make the per‑object overhead slightly higher for the many temporary Marker objects created during parsing.
families.size_meaning: n is the nesting depth (number of ``or`` levels)

families.why: Evaluation of a marker walks the parsed tree recursively (_evaluate_markers). The __slots__ change does not affect the recursive algorithm, but attribute access to self._markers now goes through a slot descriptor instead of a plain __dict__ lookup. In a deep tree the same Marker instance is accessed many times (once per recursive call), so the extra descriptor overhead could make the head version marginally slower.
families.size_meaning: nesting depth of the marker expression (number of nested 'or' groups)
